{
  "dataset_name": "loan_status",
  "model_family": "linear_svm",
  "schema_generator": "claude-sonnet-4.6",
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "debt_to_income_ratio",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of loan amount to annual income, capturing borrower's debt burden relative to earnings. Higher values indicate greater financial strain.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 4.5],
      "feature_family": "financial_burden",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Direct linear signal for repayment capacity; high ratios correlate with default risk and provide clean margin separation for SVM.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "loan_amnt / (person_income + 1.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "credit_score_normalized",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Credit score normalized to [0,1] range using training set min (418) and max (807) bounds. Higher values indicate better creditworthiness.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "creditworthiness",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Smooth normalized credit signal directly usable by linear SVM without scale distortion; strong predictor of repayment behavior.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.clip((credit_score - 418.0) / (807.0 - 418.0), 0.0, 1.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "interest_rate_normalized",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Loan interest rate normalized to [0,1] using training set min (5.42) and max (20.0). Higher values indicate riskier or more expensive loans.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "loan_cost",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Normalized interest rate provides smooth continuous signal; high rates often reflect lender-assessed risk and correlate with default.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.clip((loan_int_rate - 5.42) / (20.0 - 5.42), 0.0, 1.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "income_log_scaled",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-transformed income scaled by log of training mean income to reduce skewness. Captures income level on a compressed scale.",
      "value_range": [0.5, 2.5],
      "feature_family": "income_capacity",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Log transformation reduces extreme income outliers, creating a more linear relationship with repayment capacity for SVM margins.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(person_income) / np.log1p(79417.16)"
    },
    {
      "name": "loan_percent_income_clipped",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Loan percent of income clipped to [0, 0.62] range and scaled. Directly measures what fraction of income goes to loan repayment.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 0.62],
      "feature_family": "financial_burden",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Already a ratio feature; clipping removes any anomalies and provides a clean continuous signal for linear decision boundaries.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.clip(loan_percent_income, 0.0, 0.62)"
    },
    {
      "name": "credit_history_experience_score",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Composite score combining credit history length and employment experience, both log-transformed and averaged. Measures overall financial maturity.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.5],
      "feature_family": "financial_maturity",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Combined maturity signal captures stability dimensions; longer history and experience reduce default risk in a linearly separable way.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "(np.log1p(cb_person_cred_hist_length) + np.log1p(person_emp_exp)) / 2.0"
    },
    {
      "name": "default_history_flag",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Binary indicator for whether the person has previous loan defaults on file. 1 indicates prior defaults, 0 indicates clean history.",
      "value_range": [0, 1],
      "feature_family": "credit_risk",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Strong binary signal for prior default behavior; one of the most direct indicators of future default risk for linear SVM.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(previous_loan_defaults_on_file == 'Yes', 1, 0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "home_ownership_stability_score",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ordinal encoding of home ownership type reflecting housing stability: OWN=3, MORTGAGE=2, RENT=1, OTHER=0. Higher values indicate more stable housing.",
      "value_range": [0, 3],
      "feature_family": "stability",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Ordinal housing stability signal; homeowners tend to have lower default rates, providing useful linear margin information.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(person_home_ownership == 'OWN', 3, np.where(person_home_ownership == 'MORTGAGE', 2, np.where(person_home_ownership == 'RENT', 1, 0)))"
    },
    {
      "name": "education_level_score",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ordinal encoding of education level: Doctorate=4, Master=3, Bachelor=2, Associate=1, High School=0. Proxy for earning potential and financial literacy.",
      "value_range": [0, 4],
      "feature_family": "human_capital",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Education level correlates with income stability and financial literacy; ordinal encoding provides smooth linear signal for SVM.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(person_education == 'Doctorate', 4, np.where(person_education == 'Master', 3, np.where(person_education == 'Bachelor', 2, np.where(person_education == 'Associate', 1, 0))))"
    },
    {
      "name": "risk_composite_score",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Weighted composite risk score combining normalized interest rate (weight 0.3), loan percent income (weight 0.4), and default history flag (weight 0.3). Higher values indicate higher risk.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "composite_risk",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Single composite risk signal aggregating multiple risk dimensions; weighted combination approximates a linear projection useful for SVM margins.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "0.3 * np.clip((loan_int_rate - 5.42) / (20.0 - 5.42), 0.0, 1.0) + 0.4 * np.clip(loan_percent_income / 0.62, 0.0, 1.0) + 0.3 * np.where(previous_loan_defaults_on_file == 'Yes', 1, 0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "loan_intent_risk_score",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Semantic risk score for loan intent based on typical repayment patterns: DEBTCONSOLIDATION=0.8 (high risk, often distressed), MEDICAL=0.7 (emergency-driven), PERSONAL=0.6 (discretionary), VENTURE=0.5 (speculative), EDUCATION=0.3 (investment), HOMEIMPROVEMENT=0.2 (asset-backed). Scores reflect relative default risk by intent category.",
      "value_range": [0.1, 0.9],
      "feature_family": "loan_purpose_risk",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Loan purpose encodes borrower motivation and repayment likelihood; continuous risk encoding provides smooth signal for linear SVM without one-hot sparsity.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "age_income_stability_index",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Semantic assessment of financial stability combining age and income relative to training distribution means (age mean=27.7, income mean=79417). Scores range from 0 (young, low income) to 1 (mature, high income), with middle-age and moderate income receiving highest scores around 0.7-0.8 to avoid penalizing very high earners.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "demographic_stability",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Combined demographic stability signal captures life-stage financial patterns; continuous score provides smooth linear separability for SVM without interaction term complexity.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    }
  ]
}
